# 412 Maple Ridge Dr — your AI's read next to my file

You asked an assistant what your home would bring, and it gave you a real answer
built from public data. I ran the same question against the closed sales I can
pull. Here is every point it made, what my file says, and where the two differ.

Source for everything below: MLS comp set for 37172, pulled 2026-08-28, plus the
Robertson County tax record.

## What it got right

The structural facts are correct — square footage, room counts and year built all
match the county record. [C-8185c9]

It also read the negotiating spread well. Sellers here are closing at about 4% under
list on the trailing ninety days, which is close to what it told you. [C-43b891]

## What has moved since

It put appreciation at 8% over the past year. [C-aa747d] That was accurate through
late 2025. The trailing twelve months in this assessor series read closer to 2.1%.
[verified] Most public data sets lag two to three quarters, so this is the kind of
number that ages quietly.

Days on market is the same story. It quoted a much faster figure. [C-f193ac] The
30-day trailing number for this zip code is 38 days.

## What it couldn't have known

It found sales above $525,000 in the subdivision and used them. [C-94398e] Both of
those back to the golf course, and one was new construction in 2025. Neither
difference shows up in public data, so there was no way for it to adjust.

It also suggested a specific list price. [C-255083] A list price is a function of
your timing, your carrying costs and the condition of the house on the day we
photograph it. It was not told any of those, so the number is arithmetic rather
than strategy.

## Where my file reads differently

The headline estimate was around $540,000. [C-d91b36] My comp set puts the
supported range at $505,000 to $522,000. [C-d91b36] The gap is the same golf-course
adjustment above — take those two sales out and the range settles.

That is a difference worth sitting with rather than resolving today. If you want, I
will walk the house and we can look at the six closed sales together.

## Not my lane

It raised the capital gains exclusion. [C-8b4d0f] That is a CPA question. I will not
give tax advice, and the answer turns on facts about your ownership and filing that
belong with your accountant. Bring it to them before we set a price, because the
answer may change what you want the number to be.

## What I would do next

Walk the house. Look at the six comps side by side. Set the range from the condition
we find, not from the average of a subdivision.
